recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a future work group wants the literal FHIR-49734 wording instead of the current FHIR-41846 wording, that should be handled as a new explicit change.
issue_request: FHIR-49734 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and asked to fix the ElementDefinition.requirements short display from "Why this resource has been created" to wording such as "Why this element is defined as it is."
initial_application: Commit 28e721e2d771a64b80772835853b8b8b218c8429 for FHIR-41846 changed ElementDefinition.requirements from "Why this resource has been created" to "Requirements satisfied by this element/structure and its constraints." The FHIR-49734 Jira application comment says it had already been changed to something else better. Commit 7da8914d3dc197ecc758ea1ed409e6b9f9c1dc85, titled FHIR-49734, changed Requirements.statement instead of ElementDefinition.requirements and therefore was not a needed application of FHIR-49734 itself.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini maps elementdefinition to the elementdefinition datatype page and marks ElementDefinition normative. FHIR-I WGM May 2025 minutes record the FHIR-49734 vote and rationale that both "resource" and "created" were problematic in the old short. The current FHIR-41846 wording no longer uses either term and is more specific to requirements satisfied by an element/structure and its constraints.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the active ElementDefinition.requirements short already corrects the problematic old wording, and changing it to the literal FHIR-49734 proposal would override the existing issue-backed wording that Jira explicitly accepted at application time.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Applied issue that changed ElementDefinition.requirements to the current short display accepted by the FHIR-49734 application comment.
Seed investigation encountered FHIR-49734 because a commit with this key changed Requirements.statement, not because FHIR-49734 needed the seed source change.
